text.p: Textron Inc., a maker of aircraft, automotive and industrial products, Thursday reported record profits for the third quarter, with the gain fuelled by its acquisitions in the past year.
The company said income from continuing operations rose to $120 million, or $1.40 a share, in the third quarter, versus year-ago earnings of $104 million, or $1.20 a share.
Revenues rose 9 percent to $2.24 billion from $$2.05 billion.
"Our third-quarter performance indicates the strength of our core business segments," said Textron Chairman and Chief Executive Officer James Hardymon.

"For the past seven years, Textron shareholders have realised the benefits of the company's multi-industry strategy," he said. "We are well on our way to another record year, and are optimistic about the prospects for 1997."
The company said that acquisitions made in late 1995 and the first half of this year lifted the earnings of its industrial unit by 47 percent.

"Over the past year, Textron has made eight acquisitions, including four in Europe, which have added to the product and market capability in the Industrial, Automotive, and Finance segments," Hardymon said.
Textron's stock was off 75 cents at $87.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
